words.text: 3 Except where this regulation provides otherwise, the holder of a hunting licence may only hunt (a) the species of wild animal named in the licence; (b) using the type of equipment stated in the licence; and (c) in an area designated in this regulation for such a species, licence and equipment type.

absence.explanation: A licence authorises hunting only in the areas, with the equipment and in the seasons the regulation designates for it. Where no row designates this place for this licence, the regulation closes it.

zone1.statedAs: All that portion of the province lying north of the 57th parallel of north latitude and that part lying east of the meridian of 94 west longitude and north of the parallel of 56 north latitude;

zone2Line.statedAs: commencing at the intersection of the boundary between Manitoba and Saskatchewan and the 53rd parallel; thence east along the said parallel to the east shore of Lake Winnipegosis; thence southeasterly following the sinuosities of the east shoreline of the said lake to the north limit of Township 43; thence east along the north limit of the said township to the boundary between Manitoba and Ontario;
zone2Line.derivation: Township lines lie at least six miles apart northward from the 49th parallel, so the north limit of Township 43 is above 52.73°N, and the whole zone 2/3 line lies between that and the 53rd parallel. North Ground holds no survey geometry for it; a point between 52.70°N and 53.05°N outside GBHZ 4 is treated as undetermined between zones 2 and 3.

zone3.statedAs: All that portion of the province lying between game bird hunting zone 2 and game bird hunting zone 4;

legalAnimalClasses.criterionBlocker: M.R. 165/91 s. 25 limits the bag to one adult black bear and does not define adult. Section 26 defines a cub (20.5 kg or less) only for the prohibition on killing a female accompanied by one, so that weight is not the test of adult.

provisions.text: 3 Except where this regulation provides otherwise, the holder of a hunting licence may only hunt (a) the species of wild animal named in the licence; (b) using the type of equipment stated in the licence; and (c) in an area designated in this regulation for such a species, licence and equipment type.
2 All dates and all references to areas by means of numbers in this regulation are inclusive.
"hunting year" means the period beginning on April 1 and ending March 31;
3.3 When the word "archery" is used in the name of a particular hunting licence or in a column of a Schedule, it means that a long, recurved or compound bow may be used
3.4 When the term "all equipment" is used in a column of a Schedule, it means a rifle, shotgun, muzzleloader, crossbow or a long, recurved or compound bow may be used

9(3) The holder of a Manitoba resident second white-tailed deer licence shall not hunt white-tailed deer under authority of that licence unless the holder is also in possession of a Manitoba resident general white-tailed deer licence that is valid during the period and for the area in which the second white-tailed deer licence is being used.

10(3) The holder of a Manitoba resident third white-tailed deer licence shall not hunt white-tailed deer under authority of that licence unless the holder is also in possession of a Manitoba resident general white-tailed deer licence and a Manitoba resident second white-tailed deer licence that are valid during the period and for the area in which the third white-tailed deer licence is being used.
11(1) The bag limit is one white-tailed deer for the following types of white-tailed deer hunting licences:
11(2) The bag limit for a Manitoba resident second white-tailed deer licence and a Manitoba resident third white-tailed deer licence is one antlerless white-tailed deer.
"antlerless" means without antlers or with antlers less than 10 centimetres (4 inches) in length;

29.1 Despite any other provision in this regulation, the holder of a disabled crossbow permit who holds a hunting licence that allows him or her to hunt using a long, recurved or compound bow may also use a crossbow when hunting under authority of that licence.
3 No person shall hunt wildlife between 1/2 hour after sunset and 1/2 hour before sunrise of the following day.

10(1) No person shall hunt, dress or retrieve a big game animal or coyote or act as a guide or otherwise accompany a person hunting, dressing or retrieving a big game animal or a coyote unless the person is wearing the following items that are not covered in any way:
(a) archers hunting during an archery season;
10(3) No person shall hunt upland game birds during the general deer season unless the person is wearing the following items that are not covered in any way:
(k) hunt or kill upland game birds with a centrefire rifle, shotgun or muzzleloading firearm loaded with a single projectile;
"male", in respect of a deer, moose or elk, means a deer, moose or elk with antlers more than 10 centimetres (4 inches) in length;

3.2(1) Subject to subsection (2), when the word "general" is used in the name of a particular hunting licence, it means that a rifle, shotgun, muzzleloader, crossbow or a long, recurved or compound bow may be used to hunt in the areas and during the open seasons for which the licence in question is valid.
3.2(2) Subsection (1) does not apply to any type of general deer hunting licence or general bear hunting licence.

11.2(3) The holder of a Manitoba resident second mule deer licence shall not hunt mule deer under authority of that licence unless the holder is also in possession of a Manitoba resident general mule deer licence that is valid during the period and for the area in which the second mule deer licence is being used.

11.3(3) The holder of a Manitoba resident third mule deer licence shall not hunt mule deer under authority of that licence unless the holder is also in possession of a Manitoba resident general mule deer licence and a Manitoba resident second mule deer licence that are valid during the period and for the area in which the third mule deer licence is being used.
11.5(1) The bag limit for a general mule deer licence is one mule deer.
11.5(2) The bag limit for a Manitoba resident second mule deer licence and a Manitoba resident third mule deer licence is one antlerless mule deer.
12(2) No person who is the holder of a Manitoba resident draw archery elk licence shall hunt or kill elk except by means of a long, recurved or compound bow.

16(1) The holder of a licence referred to in section 12, 13 or 14 that authorizes a person to hunt elk in area 23 or 23A, or both of those areas, during an open season specified in Column 2 of Schedule C may also hunt male moose in those areas during that open season.
16(2) The holder of a licence referred to in subsection (1) may kill either one elk or one male moose under the authority of that licence during the open season for the licence in question.
17(2) The holder of a Manitoba resident archery moose licence may hunt or kill a moose under this section only by means of a long, recurved or compound bow.
20(1) Subject to subsection (2), no person shall kill more than one male moose during a licence year.
25 The bag limit for any type of black bear hunting licence is one adult black bear.
26(1) No person shall kill or attempt to kill a female bear while she is accompanied by a cub.
26(2) In this section, "cub" means a black bear weighing 20.5 kg or less.
(c) a person hunting black bears during the period April 1 to June 30;

8(1) No person shall place a bait for the purpose of hunting black bears or gray wolves (a) within 200 m of a public road or a dwelling; (b) within 500 m of a campground, picnic site or cottage subdivision located on Crown land;

8(2.1) A person placing a bait for the purpose of hunting black bears or gray wolves in game hunting area 23 or 23A (a) must not place bait more than 14 days before the start of the applicable hunting season; and (b) must remove the bait no later than five days after the end of the applicable season.
